\title{Refinement Steps Buy Intelligibility, Not Identity:\\
Metric-Selective Test-Time Scaling in Masked-Diffusion TTS}
\author{Anonymous authors\\Paper under double-blind review}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
A diffusion language model buys sequential computation twice: depth, paid once in
parameters, and denoising steps, rented per utterance at serve time. We ask whether the
rented kind helps every capability equally. We train an iso-parameter width--depth grid
of \Nconfigs\ masked-diffusion codec TTS models (\Nseeds\ seeds, 20--125\,M non-embedding
parameters) and sweep the refinement budget $T$ at inference only, giving a \Nsurface-point
$(w,d,T)$ surface per metric from \Nruns\ trained models. Fitting
$\mathrm{err}=E+Aw^{-\alpha}+Bd^{-\beta}+CT^{-\tau}$ pre-registered, refinement steps
attack intelligibility harder than speaker identity:
$\Delta\tau=\tau_{\mathrm{WER}}-\tau_{\mathrm{SIM}}=\Ndtau$, 95\% run-level bootstrap CI
\Ndtauci. Word error rate saturates only at $T^{*}{=}\NtstarWER$ while identity saturates
at $\NtstarSIM$. Depth and steps are \emph{not} interchangeable: the substitution form
$B(d\,T^{\kappa})^{-\beta}$ is worse than the separable form by
$\Delta\mathrm{AICc}=+\NaiccSSWER$. Steps are an intelligibility knob, not a general one.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
A diffusion language model can buy sequential computation twice. It \emph{owns} depth:
$d$ transformer blocks, paid once in parameters and then on every forward pass forever.
It \emph{rents} refinement steps: $T$ denoising passes over the same sequence, paid per
utterance and adjustable at serve time. An autoregressive model has only the first lever;
its serial cost per token is fixed by the architecture the moment training ends. If rented
serial compute substitutes for owned serial compute, a deployment can trade parameters for
steps after the fact --- but only for the capabilities that steps actually improve.

Zero-shot text-to-speech is an unusually clean probe of that question, because it separates
two capabilities that are measured by standard, independent metrics. Intelligibility is
compositional: the model must place the right phonetic content in the right order, and word
error rate (WER) reads it out. Speaker identity is representational: the model must carry
timbre from a short prompt into new content, and speaker similarity (SIM-o) reads that out.
The two need not respond to the same knob.

We train one iso-parameter width--depth grid of masked-diffusion codec language models and
then sweep $T$ at inference only, which yields a full $(w, d, T)$ response surface per
metric at zero additional training cost. Two claims were pre-registered before any run.
\textbf{H-D2}: refinement steps improve intelligibility more than identity, i.e.\ test-time
scaling is metric-selective. \textbf{H-D3}: for intelligibility, steps and depth exchange at
a measurable rate $\kappa$ --- how many step-doublings buy one depth-doubling.

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:models}
\mathrm{err}_m(w,d,T) = E_m + A_m w^{-\alpha_m} + B_m d^{-\beta_m} + C_m T^{-\tau_m}
\qquad
\mathrm{err}_m(w,d,T) = E_m + A_m w^{-\alpha_m} + B_m \big(d\,T^{\kappa_m}\big)^{-\beta_m}
\end{equation}

Both claims were registered before the first run, together with the thresholds, the
frozen sampler and the analysis plan. The answer to the first is yes and quantitative:
$\Delta\tau = \Ndtau$ with a run-level bootstrap CI of \Ndtauci, so the step exponent is
reliably larger for intelligibility than for identity. The answer to the second is a clean
no: the substitution form is decisively \emph{worse} than the separable one
($\Delta\mathrm{AICc}=+\NaiccSSWER$ for WER, $+\NaiccSSSIM$ for SIM-o) and $\kappa$ runs to
its bound, so no finite depth--step exchange rate describes this regime. The two results
together say something sharper than either alone: extra inference compute is a targeted
instrument, and it cannot be treated as a substitute for architecture.

Contributions. (i) The first per-metric $(w, d, T)$ scaling surface for speech
generation, \Nsurface\ points per metric from one training grid, released with the harness.
(ii) $\Delta\tau$ with a confidence interval, and the negative result on depth--step
substitution stated as an AICc comparison rather than a narrative. (iii) A serving
consequence measured rather than assumed: on the evaluation GPU $c_{\mathrm{layer}}$ is
flat in width at batch 1, so serial latency is $8Td\cdot c_{\mathrm{layer}}$ and the step
budget is the only latency knob that trades against intelligibility.

\section{Related work}
Masked diffusion language models are now trained at scale \citep{llada,mdlm,d3pm}, but their
scaling is reported against a single likelihood-shaped objective, so a per-capability
question cannot arise. In speech, the masked-generative recipes that made codec-token TTS
practical --- confidence-decoded parallel generation over residual codebook levels
\citep{soundstorm,maskgit} and its multi-stage successors \citep{maskgct} --- fixed a step
budget by engineering judgement and reported a single operating point; none maps error
against steps as a law. Autoregressive codec TTS \citep{valle} has begun to report scaling
behaviour, but in total parameters $N$ only \citep{llasa}, which cannot separate width from
depth and has no step axis at all; classical scaling work is likewise $N$-indexed
\citep{kaplan,chinchilla}. Test-time scaling is well studied in reasoning
\citep{testtime}, where the payoff is measured on one correctness metric; whether extra
inference compute helps different capabilities \emph{differently} is, to our knowledge,
untested in generative speech. That is the gap this abstract fills: per-metric laws in
$(w, d, T)$ for a masked-diffusion TTS model.

\section{Method}
\paragraph{Backbone and objective.}
A bidirectional (non-causal) pre-LN transformer over Mimi \citep{moshi} codec tokens at 12.5\,Hz with the
first 8 residual codebooks (2048 entries each, plus MASK and PAD). Width $w$, depth $d$,
head dimension 64, GELU MLP ratio 4, RMSNorm, RoPE, no weight tying, so the non-embedding
parameter count is $N = 12\,d\,w^{2}$. One embedding table per codebook is summed at the
input and one linear head per codebook reads out. Training is SoundStorm-style \citep{soundstorm}
coarse-to-fine masking: per example a level $l \sim \mathcal{U}\{1..8\}$ and a ratio
$t \sim \mathcal{U}(0,1]$; levels below $l$ stay visible, level $l$ is masked i.i.d.\ with
probability $t$, levels above $l$ are entirely MASK; the loss is cross-entropy on the masked
cells of level $l$ only. A phoneme prefix and a 3-second prompt of codec tokens are always
visible; there is no speaker encoder, so the backbone itself is the only identity pathway,
and no classifier-free guidance, which would add a second inference-time axis and confound
the step axis. The target length is fixed before generation from the text length and a
corpus character rate ($\Nsecperchar$\,s/char).

\paragraph{Frozen sampler.}
MaskGIT-style confidence decoding \citep{maskgit}, level by level, with exactly $T$ refinement steps per level, so
NFE $= 8T$: a cosine schedule sets how many cells remain masked after each step, tokens are
drawn categorically at temperature 1.0, and confidences are log-probabilities plus Gumbel
noise annealed $1 \to 0$ within a level; committed cells stay committed. The sampler is
identical for every config, seed and $T$ --- nothing is tuned per shape or per step budget.
Per-item generation noise is keyed so that each item sees the same noise at the first step of
every level for every $T$, making $T$ the only difference between surface points of one run.
Before any metric is computed we verify that $T$ reaches the sampler: outputs at $T{=}1$ and
$T{=}16$ must differ on more than 20\% of generated token cells.

\paragraph{Design and statistics.}
$\Nconfigs$ configs span three iso-$N$ budgets $\times$ five aspect ratios, each trained at
$\Nseeds$ seeds for 30{,}000 steps at effective batch 256 with $\mu$P \citep{mup} (base width 256, base
LR $\Nbaselr$); width transfer and depth transfer were verified by five-point LR sweeps
before the grid. $T \in \{\NTgrid\}$ is swept at evaluation only, giving $\Nsurface$ surface
points per metric from $\Nruns$ trained models. Metrics: WER (Whisper-large-v3 \citep{whisper}, greedy, the
Whisper English normaliser), SIM-o (WavLM-large \citep{wavlm} speaker-verification embedding against the
\emph{original} prompt waveform, following \citet{seedtts}), a frozen degenerate-output rule, and UTMOS \citep{utmos} as a tertiary.
Error transforms are $\mathrm{err}_{\mathrm{WER}} = \mathrm{WER}$ and
$\mathrm{err}_{\mathrm{SIM}} = 1 - \text{SIM-o}$, computed over all items including
degenerates. Both forms of Eq.~\eqref{eq:models} are fitted by weighted non-linear least
squares with 32 multi-starts; $\Delta\tau = \tau_{\mathrm{WER}} - \tau_{\mathrm{SIM}}$,
$\kappa$, and $\Delta\rho = \alpha_{\mathrm{SIM}}/\beta_{\mathrm{SIM}} -
\alpha_{\mathrm{WER}}/\beta_{\mathrm{WER}}$ carry percentile confidence intervals from a
bootstrap that resamples at the \emph{run} level --- the five $T$-points of one run share a
trained model, so resampling surface points would understate their correlation --- with
$\Nbootreps$ replicates recomputing every $T$ point.

\section{Results}
\paragraph{Steps are metric-selective (H-D2, supported).}
Fitted on all \Nsurface\ surface points, the step exponent is $\tau_{\mathrm{WER}} =
\Ntauwer$ (CI \Ntauwerci) against $\tau_{\mathrm{SIM}} = \Ntausim$ (CI \Ntausimci), so
$\Delta\tau = \Ndtau$ with CI \Ndtauci, excluding zero. The raw surface shows the same
thing without any model: averaged over the grid, going from $T{=}1$ to $T{=}16$ takes WER
from \Nwertone\% to \Nwertsixteen\% --- a factor of \NwerratioT\ on the error scale --- while
SIM-o moves only from \Nsimtone\ to \Nsimtsixteen, a factor of \NsimratioT\ on
$1-\text{SIM-o}$. The saturation steps differ accordingly: $T^{*}_{\mathrm{WER}} =
\NtstarWER$, i.e.\ intelligibility is still improving at the largest budget we tested,
while $T^{*}_{\mathrm{SIM}} = \NtstarSIM$. The power gate over shapes \Ngfour\ in all three
budgets before these tests were run.

\paragraph{Depth and steps do not substitute (H-D3, not supported).}
The pre-registered substitution form collapses: $\Delta\mathrm{AICc}
(M_{\mathrm{sub}}-M_{\mathrm{sep}}) = +\NaiccSSWER$ for WER and $+\NaiccSSSIM$ for SIM-o,
where the hypothesis required $\le +4$, and the fitted $\kappa$ sits on its bound for both
metrics, i.e.\ the exchange rate is not identified. We therefore quote no $\kappa$. The
mechanism is visible in the fits: $T$ enters with a large additive term that decays as
$T^{-\tau}$ towards a floor, whereas depth changes the floor itself; a model that forces
the two into one factor $d\,T^{\kappa}$ cannot fit both the strong depth ordering at fixed
$T$ and the strong $T$ ordering at fixed depth.

\paragraph{Shape matters, but the anisotropy ratio is not identified (H-D1, not supported).}
At $T{=}16$ the two-axis model beats the $N$-only model decisively for both metrics
($\Delta\mathrm{AICc} = \NaiccFNWER$ for WER, $\NaiccFNSIM$ for SIM-o, against a $-4$
threshold), so error is not a function of parameter count alone --- iso-$N$ shape choice
matters. The direction of the anisotropy, however, we cannot claim: $\Delta\rho = \Ndrho$
with CI \Ndrhoci, spanning zero, and the width coefficient $A$ collapses to its lower
bound for both metrics at $T{=}16$, which leaves $\alpha$ --- and hence $\rho =
\alpha/\beta$ --- unidentified. What the data do show unambiguously is a strong depth
ordering at fixed parameter count: within each budget, the deepest shape beats the
shallowest by \NdepthgainA\ (20\,M), \NdepthgainB\ (50\,M) and \NdepthgainC\ (125\,M)
points of WER, while SIM-o varies by less than \NsimspreadTsixteen\ across all \Nconfigs\ shapes.

\paragraph{Extrapolation and reliability.}
Fitting the two smaller budgets and predicting the largest gives MAPE \NmapeSIM\% for
SIM-o (versus \NmapeNSIM\% for the $N$-only model), inside the 15\% the hypothesis asked
for; WER does not extrapolate (\NmapeWER\% versus \NmapeNWER\%). Degenerate outputs ---
empty, truncated or looping transcripts under the frozen rule --- fall monotonically with
the step budget, from \Ndegentone\% at $T{=}1$ to \Ndegentsixteen\% at $T{=}16$: most of what
$T{=}1$ costs is not subtle quality but outright failures.

\paragraph{Serving corollary.}
Measured on the evaluation GPU at batch 1, $c_{\mathrm{layer}}$ is flat in width across
the whole grid (\Nclayerrange\ ms per layer for $w \in [256, 1152]$): at these sizes the
device is launch-bound, so serial latency is $8\,T\,d\,c_{\mathrm{layer}}$ and width is
free. Combined with the two results above, the allocation rule is unusually simple.
Spend parameters on depth until the latency budget binds, because depth lowers the WER
floor and width does not measurably move either metric's floor here; then spend the
remaining latency on steps, which buy intelligibility down to $T^{*}_{\mathrm{WER}} =
\NtstarWER$ but stop buying identity after $T^{*}_{\mathrm{SIM}} = \NtstarSIM$. A system
that needs identity more than intelligibility --- voice preservation with short, fixed
prompts --- can run at \NtstarSIM\ steps and reclaim
\Nlatencysaving\% of the serial latency of a $T{=}16$ configuration.

\section{Limitations and outlook}
The ceiling is \NmaxN\,M non-embedding parameters and 30{,}000 steps; every model is
under-trained by frontier standards, and the $T$ curves may flatten differently at scale
--- $T^{*}_{\mathrm{WER}} = \NtstarWER$ is a lower bound, since WER had not saturated at
the largest budget we measured. One language, one codec, one corpus, and no
classifier-free guidance: guidance is a second inference-time axis and would have
confounded the step axis, so excluding it is deliberate but it does leave the most
obvious follow-up open. The $\Delta\tau$ interval comes from resampling \Nseeds\ runs per
config, so it captures seed-to-seed variation and not the uncertainty contributed by the
single shared harness and corpus; it should be read as the pre-registered statistic it is,
not as a full error budget. $\Delta\rho$ and $\kappa$ are reported as unidentified rather
than as estimates, and no claim is made from them. Calendar and compute cuts taken:
\Ncuts. Under the pre-registered outcome classes this is class \Noutcome, and the
selectivity claim is the only positive claim the data license.

\paragraph{Reproducibility.}
The protocol, hypotheses, thresholds, frozen sampler and analysis plan were registered
before the first training run, and every gate evaluation is logged with its measured
values. The released artefact contains the harness, all \Nruns\ run records, the full
\Nsurface-point surface, the fits and the bootstrap code. Data is a $\Nhours$\,h English
subset of a public corpus \citep{emilia} with $\Nspeakers$ training speakers and 200
speakers held out; the eval set is curated only for ground-truth transcribability, a
model-independent filter. Total cost \Ngpuhours\ GPU-hours on one 8-GPU node.
